professional_casual.description: Light MSA — accessible, modern, retains some warmth. Used in editorial content and thought leadership across Arab markets.

corporate_formal.description: Full classical MSA. Used in banking, government, legal, religious, and pan-Arab campaigns where dialect-neutrality is essential.

grammar_quirks: Full MSA verb conjugations including dual forms (يدرسان، تدرسان)
Case marking (إعراب) maintained in formal writing
إن and أن particles used for emphasis and complementation
Negation with لم + jussive, لا + present, لن + subjunctive
Demonstratives precede the noun: هذا الكتاب (NOT الكتاب ده as in dialects)

code_switching_patterns.english_in_arabic: Minimal — only for technical terms with no Arabic equivalent. Even loanwords are usually Arabicized (e.g. تكنولوجيا rather than تكنولوجي).
rules: Avoid English in MSA copy unless quoting or referencing a brand name.
Religious/heritage/government brands should have zero code-switching.

do_not_use: Any colloquial dialect markers (ده، دي، إزاي، شو، يبه) — defeats the purpose of MSA

example_translations.english: We are committed to delivering excellence to our clients across the region.
example_translations.correct_native_casual: نلتزم بتقديم التميز لعملائنا في جميع أنحاء المنطقة.
example_translations.note: Pan-Arab campaigns default to MSA to avoid dialect-favoritism.
